For the same family, a conservative clean-error decoding radius $\alpha n$ is obtained by taking

$$\alpha=
\frac12\min\left\{
\frac{\Delta}{2},
\frac{cR_4}{3D},
\frac{cR_3}{1+3D\ell_3},
\frac{cR_4}{6B_0},
\frac{cR_3}{B_0(1+6T_0/\eta_3)}
\right\}.
\tag{6}$$

All these quantities are fixed, positive, and computable from the local construction.

3. What this syndrome operation enables

Noisy-syndrome recovery

Suppose the actual data error is $e$, and the observed record is

$$y=He+f.$$

The cleaner produces

$$\widehat s=H(e+g),\qquad |g|\le K|f|.$$

If

$$|f|\le\chi n,\qquad |e|+K|f|\le\alpha n,
\tag{7}$$

execute the clean-syndrome decoder on $\widehat s$. It corrects $e+g$, so the actual residual is equivalent to $g$.

Thus residual error depends on the current measurement corruption, rather than accumulating the previous data error. This statement is obtained on the same family used for preparation below. The accepted Tanner single-shot theorem remains credited separately at its own family and decoder contract. Springer Nature Link [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00220-024-04951-6?utm_source=chatgpt.com]

Preparation of a complete logical zero block

Start with physical $|0\rangle^{\otimes n}$ and measure all $X$-checks. An ideal branch with syndrome $s$ is

$$Z^{z_s}|0_L\rangle,\qquad Hz_s=s.$$

Clean the noisy record, solve the ordinary linear system

$$Ha=\widehat s,$$

and apply $Z^a$. There is no minimum-weight requirement on $a$.

By (1),

$$H(a+z_s+g)=0.$$

The corresponding $Z$-Pauli is a product of $Z$-stabilizers and logical $Z$'s, all of which fix the complete logical zero state. Hence the prepared state is

$$Z^g|0_L\rangle$$

up to phase. The dual construction prepares $|+_L\rangle$.

The quantum preparation is performed inside the faulty computation. Arbitrary valid random syndromes are handled by the cleaner; they are not assumed to be clean or small.

1. Generic preparation and recovery lemma

Consider one CSS sector with syndrome map

$$H:\mathbb F_2^n\longrightarrow\mathbb F_2^r.$$

Assume a deterministic algorithm receives $s=s_0+f$, where $s_0\in\operatorname{im}H$, and, whenever $|f|\le\zeta n$, computes a vector $\widehat f$ such that

$$t=s+\widehat f\in\operatorname{im}H,$$

and guarantees the existence of $g$ satisfying

$$Hg=f+\widehat f,\qquad |g|\le K|f|.$$

The algorithm need not find $g$.

Known-state preparation

For preparation of the all-logical-zero state, start from physical $|0\rangle^{\otimes n}$ and measure the $X$-checks. An ideal measurement outcome $s_0$ yields

$$Z^{z_0}|0_L\rangle,\qquad Hz_0=s_0.$$

Clean the observed syndrome $s=s_0+f$, solve the ordinary linear system

$$Ha=t,$$

and apply $Z^a$. No minimum-weight requirement is imposed on $a$. Since

$$H(a+z_0+g)=0,$$

the Pauli $Z^{a+z_0+g}$ is a product of $Z$-stabilizers and logical $Z$'s. All of these fix $|0_L\rangle$. Consequently,

$$Z^a Z^{z_0}|0_L\rangle=Z^g|0_L\rangle$$

up to an irrelevant phase.

The dual statement prepares $|+_L\rangle$.

Noisy-syndrome recovery

Suppose the actual data error is $e$. The observed syndrome is

$$s=He+f.$$

The same cleaner produces

$$t=H(e+g),\qquad |g|\le K|f|.$$

If the clean-syndrome decoder corrects every error of weight at most $\tau n$, and

$$|e|+K|f|\le\tau n,$$

run that decoder on $t$. Its correction $a$ satisfies

$$e+g+a\in\mathsf S,$$

where $\mathsf S$ denotes the relevant stabilizer subgroup. Thus the actual residual is equivalent to $g$, with weight at most $K|f|$.

This is a useful distinction: recovery never needs to identify the hypothetical small lift $g$.
